concerning.title: Call 911 now for signs of a severe reaction
concerning.intro: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) are emergencies. They can start within minutes or a few hours after eating.
signs: Swelling of the lips or tongue
Hives, or pale or bluish skin
Sudden drooling, inconsolable crying or unusual sleepiness
concerning.action: If your child has prescribed epinephrine, give it first, then call 911. If these signs aren't present but you're worried, call your pediatrician now.

mild.title: Stop this food and call your pediatrician
mild.intro: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] For milder signs such as a rash, diarrhea or vomiting, stop offering the new food and call your pediatrician before you try it again. Call 911 if any severe signs appear.
mild.action: Your pediatrician can tell you whether and when to offer this food again.
